# Audio decoder seed corpus

Seed inputs for the audio-decoder fuzz target and the deterministic replay
that runs the same files through `FormatRegistry`, the WAV byte-span decoder
and, on macOS, the CoreAudio readers. The same files serve as inspect
fixtures for the file-layout report. Every seed is small enough to commit,
every malformed seed is derived from a valid base generated in the same run,
and the whole directory is reproduced byte for byte by one script. The corpus
is entirely synthetic: no externally sourced media is included (see the
survey at the end).

## Directory contract

- Flat directory. Each seed is a plain container file with no tag prefix,
  named `<format>-<description>.<ext>`.
- Real extensions only: `.wav`, `.aiff`, `.aifc`, `.flac`, `.mp3`, `.ogg`,
  plus `.m4a` and `.caf` for CoreAudio-only coverage. The Sony Wave64 and
  RF64 seeds stay under `.wav` because `FormatRegistry` claims seeds by
  extension and registers no `.w64`; a RIFF-only reader is expected to
  refuse the Wave64 envelope.
- At least one valid, decodable seed per format: WAV, AIFF, FLAC, MP3, Ogg
  Vorbis, M4A (AAC and ALAC) and CAF.
- Every file is under 32 KB; the directory stays under 1.5 MB. Audio is
  0.1 to 0.2 s at 8 to 32 kHz so lossy encoders still emit several frames.
- Malformed seeds are expected to be rejected or flagged by decoders. The
  tables below record what two independent readers do with each one so a
  test can decide which seeds belong in its "decodes, so compare" branch.

## Regenerating

```sh
python3 test/fuzz/audio_decoder_seed_corpus.py test/fixtures/fuzz/audio-decoder
```

The script uses only the Python standard library and a fixed PRNG seed. WAV,
RF64, W64, AIFF, AIFF-C, the variable-blocksize FLAC and every malformed
variant are built in Python. The remaining encoded seeds shell out to
encoders when present (`/opt/homebrew/bin/flac`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/lame`,
`/usr/local/bin/ffmpeg` with `-fflags +bitexact -flags:a +bitexact
-map_metadata -1`, `/usr/bin/afconvert`); a missing encoder skips its seeds
with a notice and never fails the run. Two consecutive runs on the same host
produce identical bytes. A different encoder version changes the encoded
seeds, so regenerate deliberately and commit the new manifest with the
README.

Versions used for the committed files:

| Tool | Version |
| --- | --- |
| flac / metaflac | flac 1.5.0 |
| lame | LAME 64bits version 3.100 |
| ffmpeg | ffmpeg version 8.0 (libvorbis encoder) |
| afconvert / afinfo | macOS 27.2 (build 26B123) |
| python3 | 3.12.13 |

## Seeds

Every file in this directory is generated by Pulp's script and carries the
repository's MIT licence. Text fields (bext, LIST-INFO, ID3v2, APEv2) hold
obviously synthetic placeholders; no file embeds a host name, user name,
path or timestamp (the m4a `mvhd`/`tkhd`/`mdhd` times are zeroed).

| File | Bytes | Built by | Exercises |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wav-pcm16-mono-canonical44.wav` | 1644 | Python | Valid base: 16-byte `fmt ` immediately followed by `data` at offset 36, PCM16 mono 8 kHz. |
| `wav-pcm8-stereo.wav` | 1644 | Python | Valid unsigned 8-bit stereo. |
| `wav-pcm24-stereo.wav` | 4844 | Python | Valid packed 24-bit stereo. |
| `wav-pcm32-stereo.wav` | 6444 | Python | Valid 32-bit integer stereo. |
| `wav-float32-mono-fmt18.wav` | 3246 | Python | Valid IEEE float32 with an 18-byte `fmt ` (`cbSize` = 0). |
| `wav-float64-mono.wav` | 6444 | Python | Valid IEEE float64, 16-byte `fmt `. |
| `wav-extensible-pcm24in32-stereo.wav` | 6468 | Python | Valid `WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE`: 24 valid bits in a 32-bit container, channel mask 0x3, PCM subformat GUID. |
| `wav-bwf-bext-before-data.wav` | 2292 | Python | Valid BWF: 640-byte `bext` (602-byte fixed part plus coding history) placed before `data`. |
| `wav-list-info-heavy.wav` | 1916 | Python | Valid: eight-entry `LIST`/`INFO` before `data` and a second two-entry list after it. |
| `wav-rf64-ds64.wav` | 1680 | Python | Valid RF64: `RF64` tag, RIFF size and `data` size both 0xFFFFFFFF, `ds64` carries the real sizes and sample count. |
| `wav-w64-pcm16-mono.wav` | 1704 | Python | Valid Sony Wave64 (`riff` GUID envelope, kept under `.wav`): 16-byte GUID chunk ids, 64-bit sizes that include the 24-byte chunk header, 8-byte alignment. |
| `wav-odd-chunk-eof-no-pad.wav` | 1643 | Python | Malformed: 1599-byte `data` chunk (odd, one partial frame) at EOF with no pad byte. |
| `wav-duplicate-fmt.wav` | 1668 | Python | Malformed: two `fmt ` chunks that disagree (mono 8 kHz 16-bit, then stereo 44.1 kHz 8-bit). |
| `wav-fmt-after-data.wav` | 1644 | Python | Malformed: `data` first, `fmt ` after it. |
| `wav-data-past-eof.wav` | 577 | Python | Malformed: canonical base cut after one third of its samples; `data` and RIFF sizes still declare the full length. |
| `wav-data-size-zero.wav` | 44 | Python | Edge: complete 44-byte header, `data` size 0. |
| `wav-data-size-ffffffff-no-ds64.wav` | 1644 | Python | Malformed: `data` size 0xFFFFFFFF with a plain RIFF header and no `ds64`. |
| `wav-overlapping-chunks.wav` | 1644 | Python | Malformed: `fmt ` declares 32 bytes but carries 16, so its declared span runs into the `data` header. |
| `wav-declares-100000001-frames.wav` | 1644 | Python | Malformed: `data` and RIFF sizes declare 100,000,001 frames (200,000,002 bytes) over 1600 bytes of samples; exceeds the decode frame cap. |
| `wav-riff-header-only.wav` | 8 | Python | Malformed: `RIFF` plus a zero size, nothing else. |
| `wav-riff-size-lying-small.wav` | 1644 | Python | Malformed: RIFF size declares 100 data bytes while the `data` chunk and file carry 1600. |

| File | Bytes | Built by | Exercises |

| `aifc-none-pcm16-mono.aifc` | 1686 | Python | Valid AIFF-C: `FVER`, `COMM` with `NONE` compression and pstring name, big-endian data. |

| `aiff-ssnd-past-eof.aiff` | 454 | Python | Malformed: `SSND` declares the full sample block but the file ends after one quarter of it. |
| `aiff-comm-after-ssnd.aiff` | 1654 | Python | Order: `SSND` precedes `COMM`. Legal per the IFF rules, unusual in practice. |

## Independent-reader behaviour

Controls, run on the committed bytes: `ffprobe`/`ffmpeg -f null` (FFmpeg
8.0) and `afinfo`/`afconvert` (macOS 27.2). `flac -t` covers the FLAC
seeds. Agreement between the two readers is listed as "agree"; a
disagreement is recorded as a fact, not a failure, and is exactly what the
differential tests exist to surface.

| File | ffprobe / ffmpeg | afinfo / CoreAudio |
| --- | --- | --- |
| all 11 valid WAV seeds | decode clean, 0.1 s; `wav-extensible-pcm24in32-stereo.wav` is reported as `pcm_f24le`, 0.133 s (reads the 32-bit container as packed 24-bit) | agree except the extensible seed, read as Int32 stereo 0.1 s (the spec reading) |
| `wav-odd-chunk-eof-no-pad.wav` | decodes 0.099875 s, complains about the 1-byte partial frame | 0.099875 s, no complaint |
| `wav-duplicate-fmt.wav` | uses the first `fmt ` (mono 8 kHz 16-bit) | uses the last `fmt ` (stereo 44.1 kHz 8-bit, 0.018 s) |
| `wav-fmt-after-data.wav` | decodes 0.1 s | decodes 0.1 s |
| `wav-data-past-eof.wav` | 0.033 s then a decoding error on the partial frame | 0.03325 s, no complaint |
| `wav-data-size-zero.wav` | accepted, duration N/A | accepted, 0 s |
| `wav-data-size-ffffffff-no-ds64.wav` | treated as data-to-EOF, 0.1 s | same |
| `wav-overlapping-chunks.wav` | "no 'data' tag found", refuses | opens, reports 0 s |
| `wav-declares-100000001-frames.wav` | clamps to the file, 0.1 s | same |
| `wav-riff-header-only.wav` | refuses ("Invalid data found") | refuses |
| `wav-riff-size-lying-small.wav` | ignores the RIFF size, 0.1 s | honours it, 0.0065 s |
| all AIFF/AIFF-C seeds | decode clean 0.1 s, including `aiff-comm-after-ssnd.aiff`; `aiff-ssnd-past-eof.aiff` is clamped to the bytes present with no complaint | agree; both readers accept the truncated `SSND` silently |
| `flac-fixed-blocksize-mono.flac`, `flac-seektable-padding.flac`, `flac-variable-blocksize-verbatim.flac` | decode clean, 0.1 s; `flac -t` exit 0 | agree (`flac` reports 0 frames/packet for the variable-blocksize stream) |
| `flac-truncated-midframe.flac` | "invalid residual", `decode_frame() failed`; `flac -t` exit 1 | opens, reports 0.1 s from STREAMINFO |
| `flac-streaminfo-huge-total-samples.flac` | trusts STREAMINFO: 8,589,934.59 s; `flac -t` exit 1 ("decoded number of samples is smaller than ... STREAMINFO") | trusts STREAMINFO likewise |
| `ogg-vorbis-mono.ogg` | decodes clean, 0.2 s | 0.2 s |
| `ogg-chained-two-streams.ogg` | reports the second stream only (0.15 s) and a non-monotonic timestamp warning at the chain boundary | reports the first stream (0.2 s) |
| `ogg-truncated-page.ogg` | "End of file", refuses to open | opens, reports 0 s |
| `ogg-page-bad-crc.ogg` | "CRC mismatch!" twice, then end of file | opens, reports 0.2 s |
| `ogg-vendor-length-negative.ogg` | "End of file", refuses to open | AudioFileOpenURL fails |
| `mp3-cbr-mono.mp3` | 32 kHz mono, 0.252 s (encoder delay and padding included) | agree |
| `mp3-id3v2-xing-vbr.mp3` | tag parsed cleanly, 0.2 s (Xing gapless info honoured) | 0.252 s (gapless info ignored) |
| `mp3-apev2-footer.mp3` | 0.2865 s, treats the APE tag bytes as audio with no complaint | same |
| `mp3-truncated-frame.mp3` | 0.11225 s, "invalid new backstep -1" | 0.11225 s, no complaint |
| `m4a-aac-lc-mono.m4a`, `m4a-alac-stereo.m4a` | decode clean | decode clean |
| `m4a-aac-mdat-size1.m4a` | decodes to PCM byte-identical with the base | opens and reports the same duration, but `afconvert` output diverges from the base decode after 6900 bytes |
| `m4a-aac-co64.m4a` | byte-identical with the base | byte-identical with the base |
| `caf-pcm16-mono.caf` | decodes clean 0.2 s | agree |

## External corpora considered

Nothing in this directory comes from an external source. The candidates
below were surveyed so the hunt is not repeated; the verdict column applies
the repository licence policy (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, zlib, BSL-1.0,
CC0/public domain with a real licence text; nothing copyleft, non-commercial
or unstated, nothing over 32 KB per file). Repository contents were
enumerated from pinned trees without copying any media into this tree.

| Source | Pinned reference | Licence governing the media | Verdict and reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OSS-Fuzz `projects/dr_libs` seed corpus | google/oss-fuzz `156f862e5976b3d23828230a0a5b4fef54074d32`; `build.sh` clones `timblechmann/dr_libs-fuzzing-corpus` at `98d0fc5272d7ab1f1938a16ef16d06fca0b8e65a` | Unstated. The corpus repository has no LICENSE, README or COPYING; the adding pull request describes it only as a curated mirror of generated samples. | EXCLUDE: no licence for the media; about 30,000 files and roughly 470 MB (extrapolated). |
| `mackron/dr_libs` test media | `35b5c392cc15456736c440a68dbe073178bbffe0` | Not applicable: the repository ships no audio. `tests/README.md` points at the external `mackron/audiovectors` collection. | EXCLUDE: nothing to take. |
| `mackron/audiovectors` | `9bf8b79b5bb05ad5e398d0662f3567bd887bad7e`, no LICENSE file | Split. Collected directories (`github/`, `lynx/`, `misc/`, `unknown/`, `mpg123/`, `vorbis/`, `opus/`) are unstated. `generated/` directories carry one README sentence, "Consider these public domain", for ffmpeg-synthesised sines (18 files, 48 B to 8.3 KB). | EXCLUDE: the only grant is an informal README sentence, not a licence text, and the generated files are well-formed sines that add nothing over the synthetic seeds here. |
| OSS-Fuzz `projects/stb` | google/oss-fuzz `156f862e5976b3d23828230a0a5b4fef54074d32` | Not applicable: the project builds only the image fuzzers and fetches image suites; there is no stb_vorbis fuzzer or Ogg corpus. | EXCLUDE: nothing exists. |
| `nothings/stb` test media | `4e9b368bfc071e97206ea5c6adba68dd0cbf8897` | Not applicable: `tests/` holds `test_vorbis.c` and `vorbseek/` sources, no audio files. | EXCLUDE: nothing exists. |
| libsndfile `tests/` | libsndfile/libsndfile `396a715daeae7316f047ee220b364ab983b66df4` | LGPL-2.1 (`COPYING`). No committed audio: tests synthesise their input at run time, and the OSS-Fuzz project fabricates seeds from random bytes. No permissive grant distinct from the LGPL. | EXCLUDE: copyleft and nothing to take. |
| MediaArea `BWFMetaEdit` | MediaArea/BWFMetaEdit `5b7f3d20167092ff63dcbb5004e8dae2e88a86ea` | Not applicable: no WAV or BWF files in the repository; the website publishes binaries and documentation only. | EXCLUDE: no sample media published. |
| MediaArea `MediaConch_SampleFiles` | MediaArea/MediaConch_SampleFiles `647bb33d7887b8aaec7dd5b5110e8c96a4491226` | Unstated in the repository (no LICENSE). Related MediaConch READMEs claim CC BY 4.0 or CC BY-SA 4.0 for "digital assets" without naming this repository; the legacy LPCM files are an unattributed recording. | EXCLUDE: unstated or share-alike, and every WAV sampled is over 32 KB (44 KB to 5 MB). |
| `mackron/miniaudio` test media | `877ea4a7c2601c7b0f2a44e83dfac42e6470fea6` | `data/README`: public domain (Freesound CC0 source). `tests/_build/res/` sine WAV and headerless `.raw` files: unstated beyond the code licence. | EXCLUDE: the public-domain files are 0.5 MB to 1.8 MB; the sine WAV is 96 KB; `.raw` files have no container to decode. |
| `Tracktion/choc` tests | Tracktion/choc `8af031c2ba4f5723f4b0a5ca14e0b4984af15b0e` | Not applicable: `tests/` holds sources and a zip-reader fixture, no audio. | EXCLUDE: nothing exists. |

Nothing surveyed ships malformed audio under a stated permissive licence.
Should a qualifying file turn up later, record its source URL, commit,
licence and sha256 in the seed tables above before adding it.
